A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SymphoMotion study. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary Sections 7–8 are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative evaluations, user-study ratings, and ablations in Tables 1–3, plus qualitative generated-video comparisons in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v4 retains the original quantitative evaluations, user study, ablations, and supplementary qualitative results.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same Camera Trajectory Control and Object Dynamics Control components, conditioning mechanisms, objectives, two-stage training, and inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use RealCOD-25K for training and the same reported 100-video evaluation collection. Independent camera control, independent object control, and simultaneous control scenarios remain unchanged, including supplementary examples.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 and corresponding qualitative comparisons retain CameraCtrl, ViewCrafter, Uni3C, and MotionCtrl in their respective comparisons. The newly cited Wan-Move is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation collection, six metrics, and 1–5 user-study rating scale are unchanged. Training settings also match, including 81-frame sequences at 832×480 resolution and the same optimization procedure.

E4.justification: Section 5.3, Table 3, and Figure 7 retain the same ablations of geometric priors, 2D boxes, and 3D trajectory conditioning. Supplementary Section 8 retains the same qualitative comparisons and case analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates without repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and the qualitative results match. For example, SymphoMotion retains FID 70.47, FVD 332.50, and Box-IoU 61.88 in Table 1; supplementary examples are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), including the diffusion and flow-matching formulations and camera/object-conditioning objectives, are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theoretical results, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified camera/object control, RealCOD-25K, and superior visual fidelity and motion controllability.

C2.justification: The explanations of geometric priors and 2D/3D conditioning, interpretations of baseline behavior, and supplementary discussions are unchanged. No substantive limitations or qualifications are added or removed.

D1.justification: Implementation and annotation details, hardware, hyperparameters, supplementary interface instructions, and the project link are unchanged. Both versions report 32 H100 GPUs, batch size 32, AdamW, and the same learning-rate schedule.

R1.justification: The introduction replaces its DreamMotion citation, reference [20] in v1, with Wan-Move, reference [9] in v4. The bibliography changes accordingly, but the related-work discussion and substantive positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 removes the asterisks after Guiyu Zhang and Yabo Chen, updates the version/date header, and renumbers affected citations. The scientific prose and section structure, including the supplement, remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The author-line and citation edits cause limited text reflow, particularly in the bibliography on PDF pages 13–14. Figures 1–12 and Tables 1–3 retain their content, captions, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: v4 changes a background citation and author/header presentation while preserving the method, empirical evidence, supplementary analyses, reproducibility information, and explanatory prose. These limited edits establish no meaningful improvement or deterioration in the paper's scientific support or clarity.
